prompt: Which list contains only main features of a MANET shown in the lesson?
options: Self-forming and self-healing, fixed number of members, frequency hopping, unicast, multicast and broadcast support, quality of service
Self-forming and self-healing, dynamic number of members, frequency hopping, unicast, multicast and broadcast support, quality of service
Self-forming and self-healing, dynamic number of members, centralized administration, unicast, multicast and broadcast support, quality of service
Self-forming and self-healing, dynamic number of members, frequency hopping, permanent wired backbone, quality of service
explanation: Page 12 shows these five main features of a MANET.

prompt: Traffic is sent by parallel transmission so that all nodes are informed and no rebuild is needed after a failure. Which features are described, in order?
options: Frequency hopping; self-healing
Concurrent flooding; quality of service
Quality of service; self-forming
Concurrent flooding; self-healing
explanation: Pages 12 and 17 to 19 describe concurrent flooding as all-informed parallel transmission and self-healing as restoring the network.

prompt: Voice and video traffic compete on the same constrained link. Which main feature of a MANET addresses the performance of each?
options: Quality of service
Frequency hopping
Concurrent flooding
Self-forming, self-healing
explanation: Page 12 lists quality of service among the main MANET features; page 9 notes growing data capacity and users per network.

prompt: One message goes to a single recipient and a second goes to every node. Which delivery types fit, in order?
options: Broadcast, then unicast
Multicast, then broadcast
Unicast, then multicast
Unicast, then broadcast
explanation: Page 12 lists unicast, multicast and broadcast support; page 17 describes broadcast as all informed.

prompt: Which pairing of waveform and description is correct?
options: STANAG 4204: encrypted analog and digital voice; CNR: non-encrypted analog voice
STANAG 4204: compatible with Elbit legacy systems; CNR: compatible with the NATO waveform
STANAG 4204: non-encrypted analog voice; CNR: encrypted analog and digital voice
WMA-HC: non-encrypted analog voice; CNR: compatible with the NATO waveform
explanation: Pages 35 and 36 give STANAG 4204 as non-encrypted analog voice and CNR as encrypted analog and digital voice.

prompt: Which pairing of security layer and basis is correct?
options: Over-the-air security: SNMP v3; management security: frequency hopping and TRANSEC
Over-the-air security: AES 256 key loading; management security: frequency hopping
Over-the-air security: anti-tamper and erase; management security: TRANSEC
Over-the-air security: frequency hopping and TRANSEC; management security: SNMP v3
explanation: Page 30 gives frequency hopping and TRANSEC for over-the-air security and SNMP v3 for management security.

prompt: Which highlights belong to the HC/WMA waveform?
options: 1 MHz bandwidth, up to 4 concurrent voice sessions, up to 140 nodes
1, 2 or 4 MHz bandwidth, 7 concurrent voice sessions, up to 250 nodes
1, 2 or 4 MHz bandwidth, 4 concurrent voice sessions, up to 140 nodes
1 MHz bandwidth, 7 concurrent voice sessions, up to 250 nodes
explanation: Page 34 gives 1, 2 or 4 MHz, 7 concurrent voice sessions and up to 250 nodes for HC/WMA; page 32 gives the WB figures.

prompt: Which feature is common to both the WB and the HC/WMA waveform highlights?
options: Up to 250 nodes in a single network with automated self-forming and self-healing
Support for 7 concurrent voice sessions in the same net with analog and IP voice
A non-encrypted analog voice session compatible with the NATO waveform
TRANSEC protected, jamming resistant frequency hopping with no single point of failure
explanation: Pages 32 and 34 both list TRANSEC protection, jamming resistance, frequency hopping and no single point of failure.

prompt: Which pairing of maintenance type and activity is correct?
options: Preventive maintenance: fault isolation and repair; fault procedure: visual inspection and cleaning of the equipment
Preventive maintenance: visual inspection and cleaning; fault procedure: identification, isolation, repair, verification
Preventive maintenance: fault verification; fault procedure: cleaning of the panel and controls only
Preventive maintenance: fault identification and repair; fault procedure: visual inspection of the cables only
explanation: Pages 24 to 26 describe preventive maintenance as visual inspection and cleaning; page 27 gives the four-step fault procedure.

prompt: A technician traces a problem to one module, then replaces it. Which step comes next?
options: Fault verification, including BIT
Fault identification
Fault isolation
Cleaning of the panel and controls
explanation: Page 27 places repair verification, including BIT, after fault repair.

prompt: Which order matches the cleaning procedure?
options: Dampen the cloth with mild soap and water; inspect the exterior; remove dust with a soft cloth; clean panel and controls
Inspect the exterior; remove dust with a soft cloth; clean panel and controls; dampen the cloth with mild soap and water only if dirt is hard to remove
Remove dust with a soft cloth; clean panel and controls; inspect the exterior; dampen the cloth with mild soap and water
Clean panel and controls; inspect the exterior; remove dust with a soft cloth; dampen the cloth with mild soap and water
explanation: Page 26 gives the cleaning procedure in this order.

prompt: Which statement about the MCTR-7200HH-VS50 VA is correct?
options: It is a single-channel ruggedized vehicular adapter with a receiver and RF power amplifier covering 30 to 512 MHz at 50 W
It is a hand-held single-channel radio with a 5 W output, a GPS antenna and a handset
It is a dual-channel ruggedized vehicular adapter providing 50 W for two RT-7200 units at once
It is a single-channel ruggedized vehicular adapter with a receiver and amplifier covering 30 to 88 MHz at 50 W
explanation: Page 47 describes the VS50 VA as a single-channel ruggedized vehicular adapter with a 30 to 512 MHz, 50 W amplifier for one RT-7200 unit.

prompt: Which pairing of Nodes Information parameter and meaning is correct?
options: RSSI: received signal quality between nodes; Dist: data rate received from the remote node
SNR: received signal strength of the remote node; D.Rate: distance to the remote node
SNR: received signal quality; D.Rate: data rate received from the remote node, WMA only
Dist: received signal quality between nodes; RSSI: data rate received from the remote node
explanation: Page 56 gives these meanings for SNR and D.Rate.

prompt: Which menu options match these uses, in order: re-enabling ping after a power cycle; checking network quality with data packets; selecting waveforms for each transceiver?
options: Net Performance; Ping Enable; Transceiver Allocation
Ping Enable; Transceiver Allocation; Net Performance
Ping Enable; Net Performance; Transceiver Allocation
Transceiver Allocation; Net Performance; Ping Enable
explanation: Pages 64, 66 and 67 describe Transceiver Allocation, Ping Enable and Net Performance.

prompt: Which Net Performance option clears all the stats configured in that sub-menu?
options: Stop Test
Restore Params
Zeroize Stats
Zeroize Params
explanation: Page 67 lists Zeroize Stats as zeroizing all stats configured in the Net Performance sub-menu.

prompt: Which pairing of operational mode and use is correct?
options: OTP: maintenance mode for recovering from a technical fault; MTP: return to normal operation
OTP: return to normal operation; MTP: maintenance mode for recovering from a technical fault
OTP: normal mode with many programming cycles; MTP: one-time maintenance after a fault
OTP: loading of software updates; MTP: loading of operational parameters at the operator level
explanation: Page 68 describes OTP as the maintenance mode for recovering from a technical fault and MTP as the return to normal operation.

prompt: Which two Integrator best practices address unneeded traffic and traffic crossing into other networks, in that order?
options: Deny traffic leaking; reduce traffic
Security; reduce traffic
Reduce traffic; deny traffic leaking
Dynamic routing; deny traffic leaking
explanation: Page 70 lists reduce traffic and deny traffic leaking among the best practices of the Integrator.

prompt: In the lesson's setup examples, which values belong to the Command Post: its Site ID and its E-LynX radio Node-ID?
options: Site ID 1 and Node-ID 1
Site ID 2 and Node-ID 2
Site ID 1 and Node-ID 2
Site ID 2 and Node-ID 1
explanation: Page 22 shows the Command Post as Site ID 2, and page 74 shows its E-LynX radio as Node-ID 1.

prompt: After a repair, a technician runs the BIT and the Net Performance test and compares the Sent and Recv counts. Which step and which option are used?
options: Fault verification; Net Performance
Fault isolation; Net Performance sub-menu
Fault verification; Zeroize Params option
Fault repair; Test Results menu
explanation: Pages 27 and 67 place BIT in repair verification and describe Net Performance counting packets sent and received.

prompt: An upgrade adds video. Which integration view and which best practice should be reviewed, in that order?
options: Voice integration, then reduce traffic
Data, positions and video integration, then reduce traffic
Data, positions and video integration, then the transceiver allocation menu
Voice integration, then Ping Enable
explanation: Pages 70 and 72 present data, positions and video integration and the reduce traffic practice of the Integrator.
